findings.issue: きれい orthographically ends in い, so the parenthetical 'sem い final' is contradictory and confusing on the classic trap word; the intended point is that it lacks the inflecting i-adjective ending.
findings.current: Note que きれい usa です direto (sem い final), típico dos adjetivos-na.
findings.suggested: Note que きれい usa です direto e, apesar de terminar em い, não se conjuga como adjetivo-i — típico dos adjetivos-na.

findings.issue: Same defect as expl_pt: きれい does end in い, so '(with no final い)' is contradictory; the intended contrast is that the い is not an inflecting i-adjective ending.
findings.current: Note that きれい uses です directly (with no final い), typical of na-adjectives.
findings.suggested: Note that きれい takes です directly and, despite ending in い, does not inflect like an i-adjective — typical of na-adjectives.

findings.issue: 'sem parar de mudar' is redundant padding absent from the JP and clashes stylistically with 'parando' (parar…parar); 'fica caindo e parando' alone already renders 〜たり〜たりしている.
findings.current: A chuva fica caindo e parando, sem parar de mudar.
findings.suggested: A chuva fica caindo e parando.

findings.issue: 'constantly changing' is padding with no counterpart in the JP; 'keeps coming and going' already conveys the alternation of 〜たり〜たりしている.
findings.current: The rain keeps coming and going, constantly changing.
findings.suggested: The rain keeps coming and going.

findings.issue: Non-idiomatic English: 'keeps in this back-and-forth' is not a valid collocation (calque from pt 'fica nesse vaivém'); should be 'keeps up' or 'stays in'.
findings.current: the rain keeps in this back-and-forth of falling and stopping.
findings.suggested: the rain keeps up this back-and-forth of falling and stopping.
